historicalEvidence.dateBasis: Date on the photographer's closing slide.
historicalEvidence.observation: The stepped broad face of the Opera Tower exhibit appears behind the left edge of Shalom Meir. The 2003 night photo of the podium shows the same stepped tower and the Kirya antenna. The pair narrows the exhibit search to the Opera Tower display bed and adjacent beds on the visitor-facing side.

map.observation: The park, pool and visitor paths are mapped. The two tower platforms have no individually identified feature in the tile extract.

operaTowerControl.method: Fit horizontal sight lines to the same two ends of the highest roof edge in three archival views. The west and east picks follow the stepped wing and its opposite edge respectively.
operaTowerControl.limitation: This fit locates the adjacent Opera Tower roof approximately. It does not identify the Shalom Meir platform. The ray residual excludes errors in station geotags and camera calibration.

laterComparison.observation: The 2011 image shows Opera Tower, the gray Dizengoff tower and Azrieli. No Shalom Meir crown or drive-through can be identified in that frame or the reviewed archival panoramas. The photos leave gaps and cannot establish when the miniature moved or whether it was removed.

outstanding: Identify the end and entrance of the Shalom Meir platform in a dated wide view or aerial image with map control.
Verify the occupied footprint, facing and terrain before adding a dated or current runtime placement.
